OPIOID TREATMENT PROGRAM - PERIODIC ASSESSMENT

Patient: 41-year-old male, enrolled in OTP for methadone maintenance, diagnosed with Opioid Use Disorder, severe, per DSM-5 criteria (confirmed at intake 5 months ago). Patient voluntarily continues maintenance treatment and reports no desire to taper at this time.

Interval history: Patient presents for scheduled periodic visit, currently stable on methadone 110 mg daily. States he continues to attend dosing 6 days/week and picks up take-home doses on Sundays without incident.

Drug abuse testing review: Urine drug screen collected today; last three consecutive screens (documented in chart) were negative for illicit opioids, cocaine, and benzodiazepines; positive only for prescribed methadone. Counselor confirms compliance with testing schedule, no missed collections in this period.

Psychosocial needs: Patient reports stable housing, has re-established contact with his sister, and continues part-time employment at a warehouse. He denies any unmet psychosocial needs at this time; counseling sessions continue weekly with his assigned case manager, no gaps identified.

Necessity for visit: Visit substantiated as scheduled monthly medical review required per program protocol for continued methadone dispensing and dose management; patient also requested visit due to mild GI upset attributed to dose, wanted to discuss.

Vitals: BP 122/78, HR 76, RR 14, afebrile. Alert, cooperative, no acute distress. Pupils midsize, reactive. No withdrawal signs noted (COWS not indicated today).

Plan: Continue methadone 110 mg daily unchanged, no dose adjustment ordered this visit. Continue take-home naloxone supply, patient confirms he still has kit at home, unused. Return to clinic in 4 weeks for next periodic review; continue counseling as scheduled.

Care provided by program physician at certified OTP facility (SAMHSA/DEA certified, 42 CFR 8.11 compliant).

Record maintained in EHR available for MAC review upon request.
